reviews.text: 刚入手，流畅度和画面确实值得好评，但玩到现在，6小时通关了，打了6小时，就一把打到了最后，平衡性做的真的差，后面怪一刀秒人，正反馈真的差，商店不能刷新，删卡一次一张，3合1的意义没有特别明确，现在真不推荐入手，看后续更新吧，后面更新令人满意自会改回好评
Honestly, this is one of the better roguelike deckbuilders I've played. There is a good amount of content to keep you entertained, especially for a pretty cheap price. I would give this one a try!
Absolutely a hidden gem. Do not sleep on this game!

With all the Rougelike deckbuilders around its hard to come across one that actually does something new, and does it well! Hope this hidden gem gets more attention and that the devs release more content for it, at the moment there is no carry over/meta progression/things to unlock, but its well worth the asking price!

😺 This is not one of those... 🐶 Euh.. what? 😺 This is not one of those school project card battlers. 🐶 So what is it? 😺 This is a good and more complex card battler. If you are into card battlers, simply add this to your collection. I did the same and I enjoy playing it. Fun game!

我承认这游戏确实做出了自己的东西，队长全体（战斗buff）和板凳(手牌buff）的机制有那么点意思 那个从JRPG搞过来的相性机制我真是草了，这意味着你卡组中有2/3的牌是完全打不上伤害的。 提升卡组的能力极其有限，三连简直就是个梦，酒馆买牌由于相性的原因效果也只有1/3 又从JRPG抄了个连斗的模式，打完一波还有下一波，一排7个小火苗？ 更离谱的是从第二关开始难度暴涨，那个巫妖500血，普攻24*5是人能想出来的数值？抓不到格挡就是秒趟。 几乎所有的资源都是有限的没有任何富余，打完BOSS不回血，每关都是2个小战斗给4个面包直接见BOSS， 篝火也是需要消耗面包才能回血的，1个面包给10%回血或者30%回蓝。 打了2个小时愣是打不过第二关，切到主界面没卡组定制没新卡牌解锁项没技能调整，还得老一套重新来。 我想请开发者自己想想，玩家要是打不过咋办？
第二次体验：精简牌库已经能有效实现，牌少打的非常爽，目前已经全图鉴，希望开发者快点更新，同时希望有个官方中文Q群能讨论。图鉴里有水火两个精灵，需要困难模式分别走两条路线，以及可能需要卢卡和莱尔分别解锁。我是战士走右边带火精灵解锁了，莱尔走左边带水精灵解锁。其他成就都没啥难度。 第一次体验：右边路线已通关，左边还没有。游戏挺好玩的，就是删牌不行，卡池里弱鸡英雄太多了，局外也没有成长。希望改进。

Expectations set by being early access - no problem. Then I see the version number of 0.9.1 and realize it's probably not going to get much better, and content was pretty sparse. If you want to get this, keep in mind you might see 80% or so of the game in about an hour or two of play.

I really want to like this game, it clearly has a lot of potential, but it's very shallow at the moment, and there is little decision making on offer to make each run feel varied. A skip for now, but hopefully future updates add more depth and choice!

Seeing how I played a game like this on Mobile a few times, I was hoping this would be as interesting or as well thought out. Sadly, I was wrong. Yes, yes, Early Access, blah blah. Let's just talk about what the game has thus far and how I felt about it: I did not enjoy the time I spent with the game. To the point where I'd say I regret buying it. Visually, the game is alright. Gameplay wise, it's a lot of build up for no real pay off. Just about every Wave or Fight feels the same or plays out the same. You're going to use Heroes to either Attack for 3 element types or try and focus the two good ones. The same element as what you're attacking and what they're weak against. There is no indication you're going to attack and do half damage. You simply need to remember your early days of Pokemon Rock Paper Scissors. For the most part, any hero that doesn't have an effect are effectively useless. They're not strong enough at anything to have over another Hero who has an effect. Leader effects are often great and the only real way of doing cool setups, save for heroes with an always active sort of effect. You can basically be attacked every turn or every other turn and enemies will always have more health than your damage output. So you'll be forced into an "Attack" or "Defend/Shield" role. It gets old very quickly. Defense doesn't stay after being used so if you RNG a bunch of defense when the enemy isn't attacking, congrats, you wasted your time. Shielding is more effective when fighting less enemies but is hard to come by. And attacking is the best there is. Welcome to the entire game in a nutshell. I was stacking as many Artifacts as possible and they either gave me +Consumables or +0.1 Straight Damage. Or did something that I did not give two moldy Loafs about. After reading in their ACTUALLY helpful book of info, I figured out wtf was a Straight. And after my terrible attempts at a joke about "Gay, Bi, Etc". I couldn't help but feel as if this is worthless. None of the Artifacts I spent time collecting were really all that helpful. None of the Artifacts changed how I was playing or were strong enough to change any Meta I had in my deck of Heroes. None of the Artifacts made the game more fun to play. I found 1 Artifact that allowed me to change everyone into Leaves (Green Element) but because of it always needing MP, it wasn't always helpful. I gave up on them unless forced to take one. I started to focus on trying to save my craptastic Food resource (Loaves of bread)... which is very quickly spent during Camps for a equally weak heal of 10% per use. Well, I need 3 Heroes of the same name (But can't use the Heroes I already have 3's of because you start with them and they suck so much you want to sac them right away). So I had to play and HOPE I ended up with a selection of good Heroes that I had a Set of 3 of. It took me until Act 2 in order to RNG my way there. What was I rewarded with after doing this painstaking endeavor!? A hero who now had 1 more Equipment slot than the others. That's it. It's still as weak as it was before. Has no different card visuals. No new effects. NOTHING but 1 equipment slot. So, did I have good equipment to make use of this? No. RNG said you get 2 good equipment. One was +50% Attack, which I got when my highest attack was either 4 or 6. And another was a stick that gives AoE but lowers your damage -1. Even after using these, I was not doing enough damage to really feel as if it changed much of anything. [h2]TL;DR[/h2] Upgrading heroes did not feel worth it nor changed much about them. Hoarding Artifacts did not amount to much as they always came with extremely low bonuses. Equipment were very hit or miss and often did not feel worth it. New heroes in the Shop barely did things that warrant their purchase. No shop refreshes. No way to do something with unused/useless equipment Consumables were useful but I'm here to play cards and do combos not toss arrows and chug potions. The game will still play out useless card animations even after you've already won the battle, slowing your run and wasting time. I hoped to be entertained but did not have fun nor cared for much about the game. I'll see if the devs change things for the better in the future but right now, there are better offers out there for my time and money.

While the bones of this game are very interesting, and playing the turns is pretty fun, the lack of choices and run variation make this a lot less polished than it should be. Some early access games are pretty playable, but this feels more like a demo. You don't have time to actually collect enough units to combine 9 into one, the unit balance is all over the place, there are not enough artifacts, and they don't give you quite enough choice to be able to make meaningful build decisions; you more or less have to accept what you're given (particularly with the rare units, that you don't get to pick from 3 at all). I beat the game with both characters, and don't think I'll pick it up again until its more polished. Someday, this game could be good! But wait for it to be more polished before you buy.

游戏有自己的特色，但是必须给差评 因为一个游戏如果作者自己都不去玩，（或者作者用修改出来的阵容去设计和测试难度）甚至只凭想象来设计，虽然他也许开始会好玩，但是久而久之就让人感到反感和恶心。 我就没搞明白，像，回血，回蓝，升级卡片，删除卡片，好多个基础功能，居然共享一个事件选择，本身是随机游戏，而且比别人更复杂，加入了三连和克制机制后 随机性简直是灾难，大部分情况下 打完架只能选加血，那你卡牌构筑就被 无限期延后，甚至成型不了。 后面难度又是指数上升。最终一定会变成一个唯一的玩法，就是战斗后选择卡片，如果不是关键的就不选，前期删卡为主，回血苟住，最后看运气是否能流派成型。太复杂的构筑则直接放弃 我是玩的最简单难度尚且如此，其他难度就更不说了 建议你学一学其他游戏是怎么控制资源，别人是通过 消耗资源翻倍来增加难度，而你呢？通过限制次数来增加难度。这样整个游玩下来就毫无体验，纯粹为了难而难 说个恶心的事情，这个游戏的道具血瓶 是回复 失去生命的20% ，好家伙 我还得计算是吧？需要搞得那么恶心么？我预计游戏后面口碑会下滑，如果不是还算便宜 可能差评更多

To start with, it should be noted that I really want to give this game a positive review. This game has some great bones to offer a very fun and challenging experience. Pros: *The cards and artifacts mechanically offer a great deal of variety for a great deal of different synergies you can build towards. *The elemental triangle and straight/3 of a kind mechanic function great. This not only adds a good challenge of balancing your deck with proper element distribution but its also rewarding. Cons: *The game is horribly overbalanced. Stat values on bosses/mini-bosses are insanely high. Take for example the first boss in Golem. It has somewhere around 305 health and 4 block, as well as an average damage of 33 and a multi-turn charge attack where it does 85 damage. For reference, towards the end of stage one your deck is still pretty bad. You have had minimal chances of getting any gear to augment your cards. Your high value attack cards are probably going to be averaging around 6 attack or 8 if you got really lucky in your one summon at that point. Even at double damage for the element advantage and double stats for a run/3 of a kind, you aren't even doing decent damage under full combo. You'll be lucky if your non-element advantage cards do over even 1 damage. This leads to early bosses being 10+ minute tickle fights at best, and auto loses at worst. Also, because the damage values are so high on literally every boss, it forces you to run an extremely defense heavy build on every single run. It kills any and all build variety because you have to run some slight variation of effectively one deck to have any amount of success. *This game is extremely RNG dependant. You need an solid defensive core for your deck or you won't even get past zone one. Well at the end of every fight you have a chance for a chance to be able to add a card to your deck. If the game does grace you with a drop, you get a choice of 3 random cards. You also need your deck to be as small as possible for consistency on your draws, so if the game offers you bad cards, you're actively setting yourself up for failure by not just skipping. Even if the game does bless you with two positive rolls and you both get a card and it actually fills a role you need, the element is random which can lead to some really lopsided decks, because even a deck of good cards can fail if you have nothing but a mismatched element. Gear and artifact drops work exactly the same way. You get a couple of opportunities to visit shops where you can pick from a variety of options per zone (inns for cards and consumables twice, shops for gear and relics once). To put it short, you need to deck thin and you need a specific type of build. The game really doesnt give you the opportunities necessary because you have to chose one or the other and the opportunities are very few in occurrence. You also have to use your very limited gold for almost every transaction, so even if you are offered a really powerful card in a shop, there is a good chance you can't afford it, especially in the first two zones where it could make a world of difference. This all means most runs usually boil down to a luck-sack. *two classes with one being very noticeably worse than the other, especially when the two classes are inherently very similar, so it isn't even a matter of it being harder but with a different play-style. *four starter decks with the exact same issue as the classes. *the only form of meta progression is unlocking access to more things during your runs (cards, gear, artifacts and consumables) and given that they aren't even guaranteed to be more powerful than what you had access to prior, all it really does is saturated the pool to make it less likely that you actually get the things you really need. I like challenging games and all, but this is a bit ridiculous.

It's not heroes wanted, it's the GOTY I didn't know I wanted. This game introduced me to the roguelike deckbuilder genre. The cards are individual heroes with different classes/jobs. As a roguelike, there's no meta progression, just different artifacts to choose to start with. There will be 4 stages each run, each run is about 1 hour or more. A lot of difficulty levels. There are a lot of awesome combo possibilities. Music is beautiful and relaxing, tavern style. It has so much potential to be more awesome. Because of this game, I bought a lot of games from this same genre, but only to realize that this is the one I like the most. Got all achievements in 49 hours, but still wanting more. I do hope the devs continue to update it.

I should have returned this; even on sale this is not worth the price. I played a mobile game that was basically the exact same game only the FREE mobile game was a million times better and more engaging. (Does anyone know the name of it??? I want to play it again but I can't remember what it's called. Tri-something. Let me know in the comments if you know!) This game feels very lazy. I hate saying that but I have to believe the person who made this game either made the mobile game or is ripping it off. Either way, there's really no excuse for how shallow, ugly, and clunky this is - period for the price, but especially given that the mobile game that it is clearly based on is so comparatively well made. There are such simple things here that are missing - like there's no way to tell how powerful a card is until you get it in your deck and then sort it by tier. The cards had different color banners under the names but I couldn't seem to figure out what the colors indicated (in terms of rarity, or perhaps class/type?). The artifacts don't change the game play in any fun or significant way, and the way the whole upgrade system works, it's best to just get a few powerful cards and upgrade them (meaning, your best path is to literally just have like six cards rather than build up an interesting deck of 20 or so cards). The game doesn't force you to take cards so there's no real strategy with deck management in that regard. You can get a few cool combos going (like having counterattack activated on a card that deals damage three times and also has AOE attack, that was fun) but there's no real strategy in it. Any powerful cards will do. There's no exciting or challenging synergy between cards, items, artifacts, and equipment. Every run feels exactly the same. The lack of in-game tutorial is also a problem. Even though I had played a game with extremely similar mechanics before, even I had to figure some stuff out by just trying it out. It seems there might be a translation issue at play; many of the descriptions are worded a bit confusingly. If this was like, $3-5, it still wouldn't be a good game but it might be worth the price to kill time. But at $20 this feels like a ripoff, to the point that I'm offended by the price. And ultimately, this $20 game just made me want to go play a free mobile game instead. I think that says it all. To be fair, I haven't played that long (my playtime is somewhat bloated by the fact I left the game running on accident while distracted, hence me missing the return window) and I've only just manage to beat the first world on Normal difficulty. I know more things will unlock and possibly make the game better or more interesting. But I doubt it, and also it doesn't excuse how unimpressive my 4ish hours of actual game play so far have been. But I'll update my review if that is the case (if I bother to continue to play at all).

Heroes Wanted is a deck-building roguelike developed and published by Gameplete that delivers a refreshing spin on the genre by combining tactical card battles with elemental strategy and poker-inspired mechanics. Rather than focusing purely on collecting increasingly powerful cards, the game challenges players to carefully assemble teams of heroes whose abilities complement one another through positioning, elemental affinities, and specialized combinations. This design creates a combat system that rewards thoughtful planning over brute force, making each encounter feel like a strategic puzzle instead of a routine exchange of attacks. The core gameplay revolves around recruiting heroes, constructing an efficient deck, and adapting to the unpredictable nature of procedurally generated adventures. Every run introduces new opportunities to acquire heroes, equipment, relics, and consumable items that can dramatically alter the direction of a campaign. Heroes belong to different elemental types, and understanding how these elements interact becomes just as important as choosing which cards to play. On top of that, the poker-inspired mechanics encourage players to create combinations such as matching sets and sequences, adding another layer of tactical depth that distinguishes the game from many traditional deck-building roguelikes. Customization plays a major role in maintaining the game's replay value. Hundreds of hero cards, numerous artifacts, and a wide assortment of equipment allow players to experiment with vastly different strategies across multiple runs. Some builds focus on overwhelming offensive power, while others emphasize defensive synergy, elemental reactions, or carefully timed ability chains. Because each expedition offers randomized rewards and branching decisions, no two playthroughs unfold exactly the same. The need to constantly adapt to available resources keeps the experience engaging and encourages players to discover creative combinations they may not have considered before. Heroes Wanted also succeeds in making its layered mechanics approachable. The basic rules are easy enough for newcomers to understand, but mastering the interaction between hero placement, elemental advantages, equipment bonuses, and card combinations requires practice and experimentation. As players become more familiar with these systems, the strategic possibilities expand significantly, making later runs increasingly satisfying. The gradual learning curve ensures that progression feels rewarding rather than overwhelming, giving players room to improve with every failed or successful adventure. The presentation complements the gameplay with colorful fantasy-themed artwork and a clean user interface that prioritizes readability. Hero illustrations are distinct enough to give each character personality, while visual effects remain clear during combat without becoming distracting. Menus are well organized, making it relatively easy to manage growing collections of heroes, artifacts, and equipment even as the complexity of each run increases. Although the visuals do not aim for cutting-edge realism, they effectively support the game's strategic focus while maintaining an appealing and lively atmosphere. Replayability is easily one of the game's strongest features. Randomized encounters, varied enemy compositions, unlockable content, and countless deck-building possibilities encourage players to return for repeated attempts. Each failed run provides valuable lessons that influence future strategies, while successful runs often inspire players to explore entirely different combinations of heroes and relics. This constant sense of experimentation gives the game lasting appeal and helps prevent the experience from becoming repetitive. The game is not entirely without flaws. Since progression relies heavily on randomized rewards, some runs can feel more favorable than others depending on the cards, equipment, and artifacts that become available. Players who prefer complete control over their builds may occasionally find luck influencing their overall success. Additionally, the growing number of mechanics can require some patience before everything fully clicks, especially for newcomers unfamiliar with modern deck-building roguelikes. However, these issues are relatively minor compared to the depth and flexibility the game ultimately provides. Heroes Wanted stands out as an enjoyable and well-designed strategy game that successfully blends roguelike progression with inventive deck-building mechanics. Its emphasis on elemental interactions, creative card combinations, and meaningful customization gives every playthrough a unique identity while providing enough depth to satisfy players who enjoy careful planning and experimentation. Although randomness occasionally introduces uneven difficulty, the strong tactical gameplay, excellent replay value, and rewarding progression make it a worthwhile experience for fans of strategic card games and roguelikes alike. Rating: 8/10

Heavily relying on the 3 element countering system - your attacks are half power against counter element and double power against the one you counter. It's a nice challenge to balance all of your resources and options to make the optimal turn, and the artifacts/upgrade systems are traditional so they accomplish what they came for.
